correctness.rationale: An Euler tour in the binary order-two de Bruijn multigraph is equivalent to a single cyclic word; balance gives a=a′, b=b′, a+d=b+c and the non-isolated support must be connected. This equivalence includes n=1 and n=2 because the vertex overlaps are periodic. With both bridges present, put p=min(a,b), q=|a−b| and s=min(c,d); the length is u+v+4p+3q+2s, with one choice of bridge ordering at q=0 and two at q>0. This yields the four-vertex contribution z^4(1+z^3)/[(1−z)^2(1−z²)(1−z³)(1−z⁴)]. With only one bridge, the opposite loop must be absent, giving twice the triangle series; with no bridges there are only the alternating and two constant families. Their sum is the claimed rational function. Its degree-zero polynomial part affects only n=0, and the uncancelled primitive third and fourth poles force period divisible by 12. The fifth-order pole has coefficient 1/12, giving 1/288 on n^4. The code maximum is one per attained class. Independent literal enumeration through n=18 and formal-series numerator recovery through degree 60 matched (python3 /workspace/reproduce_reviews.py 1).
